resources.string: See another phone\'s screen and control it by touch, on the same Wi-Fi, with no account or server.
Screen sharing is running on this device.
Use this phone to see the other device\'s screen and control it directly by touch.
Let a trusted device see and control this phone. A notification stays visible the whole time and you can stop at once.
No ads, no accounts. Video and text are never recorded. The link is encrypted (TLS) between your two devices only.
Ready to share, waiting for a trusted device.
Screen sharing stopped. Tap to approve again.
“%1$s” wants to control this phone. Verification number: %2$s

“%1$s” wants to see and control this screen.

Verification number: %2$s
Make sure the same number is shown on the other device.

Device fingerprint: %3$s

Allow only if this is your device.
Android will ask for your consent. If offered, choose “Entire screen”, not “A single app”, so you can move between apps.
Sharing is on, waiting for a trusted device.
Screen capture stopped (by the system or the user, or the device was locked). Android needs your approval again.
On the controlling phone: open NITAAQ Mirror → Control another device → Scan QR code.
The code expires in about %1$d min. It is replaced after 5 wrong attempts.
Needed for touches, Back and typing. Settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps (or Installed apps) → NITAAQ Mirror → turn on.
If the switch is greyed out (Restricted setting)
Open App info → ⋮ menu (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then come back and turn the service on.
For the sharing notification, its Stop button and pairing requests.
Makes it less likely that the system stops sharing in the background (Battery → Unrestricted / Don\'t optimize).
Not on Wi-Fi. Both devices must be on the same network.
Android asks every time sharing starts; it cannot be stored permanently.

Android limits: banking apps and protected content may appear black (FLAG_SECURE); this cannot be bypassed. The app never bypasses the lock screen, PIN or fingerprint. After a reboot, sharing must be started and approved by hand.
This phone is not on Wi-Fi. Connect both devices to the same network.
Devices you paired with from this phone; connect without a code.
✓ means the device is visible on the network right now.
On the other device: Share this device → Start screen sharing. A QR code appears.
Type the address and code shown under the QR code on the host.
Check the address and that the code has 8 digits.
Device not found. On it, open Share this device and start sharing.
Unpaired devices on the network: %1$s. Scan the QR code shown on them to pair.
Can\'t connect? Make sure both devices are on the same network (not a Guest network), that the router has no AP/client isolation, and that sharing is running on the other device.
Point the camera at the QR code shown on the host.
This is not a NITAAQ Mirror pairing code.
Camera permission denied. Use manual entry, or allow the camera in the app settings.
Could not start the camera. Use manual entry.
Auto: starts fast, lowers bitrate or resolution under network pressure
Type here in Arabic or English
Text is sent to the selected field on the remote device. Or tap the field in the picture and use its own keyboard by touch.
No text field is selected on %1$s. Tap the field in the picture first.
The selected item on %1$s is not a text field.
This is a password field: text is not sent to it from here. Type with the keyboard of %1$s by touch.
This field does not accept text this way. Type with the keyboard of %1$s by touch.
Make sure the same number is shown on the host, then tap “Allow” there.
Screen sharing stopped. Open the app on %1$s and approve sharing again.
%1$s removed trust for this device. Pair again.
Another device connected to %1$s, so this session ended.
Touch control is off on %1$s. Turn on the NITAAQ Mirror service in Settings → Accessibility.
The system turned off the screen of %1$s. Tap “Wake screen”.
%1$s is locked. The lock screen may look black in the stream; the app never bypasses the lock.
No new frames: capture or encoding stopped on %1$s.
No new frames: the network is slow or dropping.
Screen sharing was not approved. Tap “Start screen sharing” and approve; choose “Entire screen” if offered.
Could not open the network port on this device. Restart the app and try again.
Video encoding stopped on this device. Tap “Approve sharing again”.
Can\'t reach %1$s. Make sure both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, that the router does not isolate devices (AP/client isolation or a guest network), and that sharing is running on the other device.
The connection to %1$s was lost and did not come back. Check Wi-Fi on both devices and that sharing is still running.
Wrong pairing code. Check the code shown on the host and try again.
Too many wrong attempts; the host made a new code. Use the new one.
%1$s refused the connection: this device is not trusted there (trust removed or request denied). Pair again.
Pairing is not open on %1$s. Open “Pair a new device” there and try again.
The identity of %1$s does not match the saved one (maybe the app was reinstalled there). For your safety, no connection was made. Remove it from trusted devices and pair again.
The app versions on the two devices are not compatible. Install the same version on both.
Devices allowed to control this device
Removing trust ends that device\'s session immediately and blocks it until it pairs again.
Applied on the host when connecting. Responsiveness first.
Rotate to match the remote screen
Keep the screen awake during a session

Prevents the screen timeout while a device is connected (official FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON). Uses more battery, does not prevent a manual lock or the power button, and is no guarantee against a faulty display.
Lets your paired device perform touches, Back and typing on this phone during a sharing session only. It does not record screen content or text.
